_readme: Portfolio demo profile: route tickets for the fictional company Nimbus3D to the team that should own them.
product_context: Nimbus3D, a SaaS platform for 3D virtual property tours used by real-estate developers and their sales teams (tickets come from clients and internal staff)
category_rubric: business_team = commercial matters: quotes, pricing, contracts, renewals, invoices, POs, refunds, credits, discounts, partnerships, case studies; developer = something in the software is broken or wrong and needs a code fix: errors, crashes, failing APIs, integrations, webhooks, wrong data shown, performance regressions, browser or device-specific bugs; support_team = helping a user use the product or their account: how-to questions, logins, passwords, 2FA, adding or removing users, exports, training, account status; product = ideas and decisions about what the product should do: feature requests, UX or layout feedback, roadmap questions, questions about why a feature changed or was removed; qa_automation = testing work: failing or flaky automated tests, CI test failures, regression runs, writing test cases, updating test baselines, reproducing a reported bug, test environments.
sentiment_rubric: angry = hostile or threatening language, ALL CAPS, ultimatums, words like disaster or unacceptable; frustrated = annoyed or under pressure but civil; neutral = matter-of-fact; positive = thanks or enthusiasm. Urgency alone is not anger.
priority_rubric: P1 = down or wrong for many users or on a live site, security or account suspension blocking a business, money charged wrongly with an ultimatum; P2 = broken or blocked for one client, team or flow with real impact, commercial requests with money or a deadline attached, release-blocking test work; P3 = how-to questions, feature ideas and roadmap questions, cosmetic issues, nice-to-have tasks.
example_message: Unit availability in our tour hasn't updated since the inventory sync failed overnight; three sold units still show as available.

example_result.summary: Overnight inventory sync failed, so sold units still show as available in the tour. Needs a fix to the sync.
